answer: Sybil defense can sit on a scarce identity ledge: each agent must lock a sizable bond against a unique TPM-backed device key that can speak for only one live account. Every epoch, a trellis of randomly sampled peers issues fresh nonces and checks that the same hardware still signs; a missed or conflicting reply slashes the bond to zero. Spawning N phantom identities therefore requires N distinct devices and N posted bonds, a linear outlay that steepens whenever trusted chips are as scarce as a clear route through flooded karst.
